summary: # How to Create Balloons and Plush Ponies in Marvelous Designer? p02 Part Two Plush Pony Production Tutorial ## Introduction Welcome to our second tutorial, where we will learn how to create a movable pet horse using a non-bonded bone structure. In this video, we will go through the steps of designing and animating a plush pony in Marvelous Designer. ## Materials and Preparation 1. **Bottom Mold Creation** I first made a very simple bottom mold and then created a movable bone frame using a key needle. After that, I covered the bone frame with the original bottom mold and constructed a movable cotton board with holes. 2. **Setting Up the Mold** I poured in the bottom mold that I had made in advance and changed its material to translucent. Next, I created a round board that matches the size of our bottom mold's body. The material for this board was adjusted to non-transparent, and I increased its length and thickness to 500, adjusting its bending force to 0 to form a cylinder. This cylinder will serve as the bone frame. 3. **Filling the Mold** I filled the cylinder into the body of our bottom mold and continuously copied out the cylinder to completely fill this bottom mold. This example uses the MD2025 version. ## Adding Movable Parts 1. **Stem Parts Addition** We will add a few more stem parts to the areas that need to move as part of the body. If the side part appears too flat, consider turning the stem into an oval shape to give the bottom a fuller appearance and reduce the chances of leaking. 2. **Skeleton Construction** Since it is a skeleton, the stem should not exceed the surface of the bottom mold; otherwise, it will alter the mold's shape. I added two panels to each leg of the horse for its skeleton. If the edges of the stem are too sharp, a slight bend can soften the shape of the bottom mold. 3. **Deleting the Bottom Mold Model** After constructing the skeleton, I deleted the model of the bottom mold and created an animation layer for all objects. I recorded an animation, bringing back the skeleton of the rabbit and the horse for animation. ## Animation Key Points 1. **Setting Key Points** We deleted all the sensory points except the first one and rebuilt the sensory points for all objects. I also rebuilt the final sensory point for the zero point when the horse is still. The animation is extended to point number 20 to start creating motions for the horse. 2. **Animating Movements** I raised the horse's legs slightly at the point set by the 20-point pin. I made it perform a movement resembling a horse flying on a bird's nest. A key point was added, but I wasn't satisfied with the movement, so I adjusted the neck and added a new 20-point pin to cover the original key points. 3. **Adjusting Movements** After pulling the progress bar to the 40-point mark, I initiated the second key movement to have the horse run. The points in between will automatically create smooth transitions, resulting in a more refined animation. Continuous adjustments were made to enhance the naturalness of the movements. ## Final Adjustments and Simulation 1. **Simulation Settings** I adjusted the simulation properties, setting gravity to 0 to prevent the fabric from falling. The fineliner strength was increased to avoid excessive elasticity, while bending strength was adjusted to 100 to minimize small wrinkles. 2. **Recording Animation** I recorded the animation again while ensuring the inner board of the horse is moved delicately. The simulation time was extended for more detail, and adjustments were made to refine the appearance of the horse. 3. **Creating the Outer Appearance** I started constructing the outer appearance of our plush pony using a 3D pen. First, I drew a middle line to ensure symmetry.
